statement: Every vector b in the column space comes from one and only one vector x_r in the row space. From the row space to the column space, A acts as an invertible (r by r) map.
quotes: Every vector b in the column space comes from one and only one vector
From the row space to the column space, $A$ is invertible.

statement: The orthogonal complement of a subspace V contains every vector perpendicular to V. The nullspace complement N(A)^perp is exactly the row space C(A^T).
quotes: The orthogonal complement of a subspace V contains every vector that is perpendicular to V
We conclude that the nullspace complement $N ( A ) ^ { \perp }$ is exactly the row space

statement: Because the row space and nullspace are orthogonal complements, every x in R^n splits uniquely as x = x_r + x_n, a row space component plus a nullspace component.
quotes: every x can be split into a row space component
Each x is the sum $x _ { r } + x _ { n }$ of a row space vector

statement: The orthogonal complement of a subspace V is denoted V^perp, pronounced "V perp".
quotes: This orthogonal subspace is denoted by $V ^ { \perp }$ (pronounced "V perp").

statement: N(A) is the orthogonal complement of the row space C(A^T) in R^n, and N(A^T) is the orthogonal complement of the column space C(A) in R^m. This is the perpendicularity of the four subspaces.
quotes: This perpendicularity of subspaces is Part 2 of the Fundamental Theorem of Linear Algebra.
$N ( A )$ is the orthogonal complement of the row space $C ( A ^ { \mathrm { T } } )$
